notes: Generated by tools/tubuild.py create, then reconciled to shared declarations, eager ROM-order emission, one source-level destructor, real Cup state member methods, and the adjacent factory tail.
The eight State* names are explicit class-anchored inferences from PMF order and behavior; the ROM proves their class identity and order, not their exact original source spelling.

Focused verification is 32/32. The former nine-word StateShuffle residual was NOT scratch-register encoding, as an earlier note in this file claimed. Six of the nine words were a different addressing-mode shape: the ROM re-materialises `this + 0x5400` at the read-modify-write site and addresses through [rN,#0x5c] / [rN,#0x5e], while the reconstruction cached that base in a local (`char *state = c + 0x5400;`) and then CSEd the FIELD address into [rN,#0]. `#pragma opt_common_subs off` is in force over this function and cannot undo it, because the CSE was performed by the source, not by the optimizer. Three source-level edits close it, all inside the `uu == 0x8000 ... else if` block: (1) drop the cached base at the store site and respell the full offsets `c + 0x545c` / `c + 0x545e`, which makes mwcc re-materialise `add rN, r4, #0x5400`; (2) negate in place as a statement (`vv = -vv;` then store `vv`) rather than storing `-vv`, which orders `rsb` before the base `add` and colours the value register the ROM's way; (3) spell the increment as a plain read-modify-write (`*(u16*)(c + 0x545c) = *(u16*)(c + 0x545c) + 0x8000;`) rather than `+= 0x8000`, because compound assignment is exactly what makes mwcc CSE the field address. The two loads earlier in the same block KEEP the cached `state` base -- the ROM shares one base register across them. Measured, not reasoned: cached-base + compound += gives 9 differing words; a `(long long)(int)` launder through the full offset gives 0x728 (eight bytes over, it forces a literal-pool address); a freshly declared inner base local plus a plain RMW gives 6; the form above gives 0.

The same three edits were applied to the legacy shard src/func_ov006_020df5b8.c, which had never carried a `complete` marker in config/arm9/overlays/ov006/delinks.txt. It compiled to 0x728 bytes before and byte-matches at 0x720 after (tools/match.py, 2004/b56), so the marker was added before the shard was superseded by this TU.
